messages:
Sam: Quick sync — I sketched a proposal for a lightweight autoscaler for Reserved GPU clusters. Goal: keep tail-latency for latency-sensitive tenants while lowering amortized cost for batchy tenants. Two core ideas: 1) split admission into fastpath (p95-driven, prewarmed nodes) and slowpath (best-effort cold starts + elastic slots), 2) introduce transient "burst credits" ledger so tenants can spike without forcing long-lived capacity. Thoughts?

Liam: +1 to separating fastpath vs slowpath. Curious about the admission boundary: where does the fastpath decision live? Control plane or operator?

Sam: Thinking control plane decides admission policy intent (SLO, reserved QPS), operator enforces via simple admission tokens and prewarm allocation. Rationale: control plane has tenant metadata and budget; operator has node lifecycle. Keep operator dumb(er) to simplify upgrades.

Anya: Question: how do we prevent oscillation where tenants burn credits, trigger node spinups, then credits run out causing thrash? Need hysteresis on spinup and a decay for credits.

Priya: Agree. Proposal: credits accrue based on committed reserved capacity and steady-state usage, decaying with a half-life (e.g., credits *= 0.9 every 5m). Also enforce a soft cap and a hard cap. Soft cap -> notify + degrade preference, hard cap -> throttle.

Liam: Can we see a minimal config sketch? I want to see how SLOs map to admission rules.

Sam: Sure — sketch DSL we debated: 
```
pos: {
  tier: "fastpath",
  slo: { metric: "p95_latency_ms", target: 150 },
  reserved: 4,            # GPUs guaranteed
  prewarm: { min_nodes: 1, probe_cooldown: 30s }
}
burst_credits: {
  accrual_rate: "10 credits/hour",
  soft_cap: 100,
  hard_cap: 300,
  decay: "0.9 per 5m"
}
admission_policy: {
  fallback: ["compatible-quantized", "lower-batch"]
}
```
This maps to control-plane intent. Operator enforces by holding N prewarm containers and a small admission token bucket per tenant.

Anya: How do we measure credit accrual fairness across tenants when packs share nodes? Attribution will be noisy.

Priya: Use token accounting at admit-time. Every fastpath admit consumes X credits proportional to gpu-time-estimate. For shared nodes, reconcile per-tenant usage by sampling (like existing billing sampler) and reconcile weekly to adjust accrual rates. Not perfect but practical.

Liam: What about placement constraints — affinity/anti-affinity — could block efficient packing and defeat cost goals. Any plan?

Sam: We should surface a placement hint score from control plane: a small vector [affinity_score, thermal_score, frag_score]. Operator uses a greedy packing scorer that weights these. If affinity_score high for tenant, operator tries to pack but will fallback after timeout to a relaxed packing to avoid stalls.

Anya: Observability: we need per-tenant metrics: credit_balance, admit_wait_time, node_spins, p95_latency-by-route. Also traces for admit flow.

Liam: And a circuit-breaker when cloud under pressure (slow node spinup): degrade fastpath to slowpath automatically. How do we trigger?

Sam: Operator exposes node_spinup_latency and free_gpu_percentage metrics. Control plane defines thresholds (e.g., spinup > 60s && free_gpu < 5%) -> temporarily reduce fastpath admission rate by 50% and start warm-provisioning smaller burst pools.

Priya: Edge-case: tenant A noisily hogs burst credits by sending many tiny requests — we should meter at token-granularity and require a min-credit-per-admit to prevent micro-attack. Also add a per-tenant rate-limiter at the edge.

Anya: One more: upgrade story. If operator is dumb, control-plane schema changes must be forward/backward compatible. We should default unknown fields and keep operator with v1 admission contract for a long time.

Sam: Agreed. Plan next steps: 1) prototype control-plane policy protobuf + simple operator token-bucket shim (2 weeks), 2) implement observability hooks and sampling-based reconciliation (week 3), 3) canary with a small set of tenants on a single shard (week 4).

Liam: Sounds good. Can we add a short playbook note: what to do if credits leak and we observe throttling?

Sam: Add to playbook: immediate steps: read credit_balance, check sampling reconciliation logs, toggle manual credit infusion (admin API), scale prewarm nodes if needed, rollback policy changes. We'll draft the playbook in docs.

orch-bot: deploy:policy-proto v0.1 pushed to staging (sha: abc123). Tests: admission unit tests passing.

Priya: Nice — I'll take the proto + reconciliation work. Anya can own observability. Liam, want you on operator shim and packing scorer?

Liam: Happy to. I'll start a PR with the greedy scorer and a simple cooldown heuristic.

Sam: Thanks all. I'll write up the short RFC follow-up summarizing decisions and owners.
